primary_blockers.title: Enterprise Sales & Contract Gates
primary_blockers.description: No self-serve signup or public developer sandbox exists. Getting credentials requires scheduled sales demos, enterprise MSAs, and annual commitments of $10k–$50k+.
primary_blockers.impact: High. Blocks autonomous agent provisioning. Requires 'Bring Your Own Credentials' (BYOC) pattern.

primary_blockers.title: Business Verification & App Review
primary_blockers.description: Requires legal entity validation (DUNS, certificate of incorporation), app privacy policy review, screencast demonstrations of end-user UI, and long approval queues.
primary_blockers.impact: High. Sandboxes exist for testing, but production write access requires rigorous institutional compliance.

primary_blockers.title: UI-Only Consumer Silos (No Public API)
primary_blockers.description: End-user applications built with consumer web interfaces that expose no public REST endpoints or developer API tokens.
primary_blockers.impact: Critical / Hard Block. Requires either browser automation (DevTools/Puppeteer) or substituting with underlying infrastructure (e.g. Google Vertex AI).

primary_blockers.title: Financial Compliance & Underwriting
primary_blockers.description: Requires formal commercial banking underwriting, PCI-DSS compliance audits, US corporate entities, or AWS SigV4 signed authorization.
primary_blockers.impact: Medium-High. Restricts deployment to authorized merchant accounts.

macro_patterns.title: Auth Polarization: Bearer Tokens in Infra/AI vs OAuth2 in B2B SaaS
macro_patterns.summary: 58% of apps rely on Bearer API Keys / Tokens, which enable zero-click agent invocation. In contrast, 34% mandate OAuth2 (dominating collaborative CRMs, Helpdesks, and Ad networks) where user delegation and token refresh loops are required.

macro_patterns.title: 68% Self-Serve Accessibility, But 32% Blocked by Commercial Paywalls
macro_patterns.summary: Developers can self-serve credentials for 68% of tools within minutes for free or on trials. However, 22% require paid plans (e.g. Aircall, GoHighLevel, SE Ranking), and 10% are strictly partner-gated behind enterprise sales calls.

macro_patterns.title: The Ad Network & Enterprise Gate: Business Verification as the #1 Moat
macro_patterns.summary: Advertising platforms (Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Pinterest) represent the highest friction category: not because their APIs are lacking, but because enterprise trust verification, app review, and legal compliance gate live production.

macro_patterns.title: The Native MCP Wave: 26% Already Support Model Context Protocol
macro_patterns.summary: More than a quarter of surveyed apps (including cutting-edge tools like Devin, Consensus, TranscriptAPI, Otter, Firecrawl, Supabase, GitHub, and Sentry) already provide native or official MCP servers, proving that agentic protocols are standardizing rapidly.

macro_patterns.title: The CLI & Local Fallback: 2% of Essential Tools Have No HTTP API
macro_patterns.summary: Key open-source developer utilities like Sherlock and Mermaid CLI have no cloud REST API. Agent toolkits must accommodate local container execution alongside HTTP REST and GraphQL.
